newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OPEC FORMALLY ENDORSES 6-MONTH OUTPUT FREEZE.
newsitem.headline: OPEC FORMALLY ENDORSES 6-MONTH OUTPUT FREEZE.

text.p: OPEC ministers formally endorsed on Thursday their decision to freeze output quotas for the rest of the year, Libyan oil minister Abdullah Salem al-Badri told reporters at the end of the OPEC meeting.
On Wednesday the ministers agreed to stick to the current 25.033 million barrels per day ceiling and vowed to adhere to their individual output allocations.
Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said that OPEC would next meet in Jakarta, Indonesia on November 26.
Saudi Arabia's Ali bin Ibrahim al-Naimi told reporters that the agreement was "excellent".
He also said that he wanted to see oil prices go up. "We want to see it (oil price) higher".
Asked about members' adherence to quotas, Naimi said: "There was reconfirmation of that (production discipline)".
OPEC output is currently running about 2.0 million bpd above its agreed production ceiling as a result of excess supply by some members.
